text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Finnish and Russian transport ministers failed to reach agreement in talks on Monday on fees levied on cargo trucks between the two countries.
- Finnish political parties and trade unions have become less supportive of EMU within the last years, particularly the Centre Party which has moved from EMU-neutral to negative.
- Flexible performance-based pay is how Finland could retain jobs in EMU, research shows.
- Police have confiscated about 3,000 litres of illegal home-made spirits from a pensioner in Rauma. Some of the alcohol came from the U.S.
- Luciano Pavarotti's concert in Helsinki next year sold out in one hour.
KAUPPALEHTI
- New grouping of state-owned defence industry companies Puolustusvaline Oy will have net sales of about one billion markka and will export about one fifth of output.

- Hotel and restaurant chain Arctia, part of Alko-Yhtiot which runs the state alcohol retail monopoly, takes over two Hotel Inter-Continentals in Helsinki. Managing director says quality of Finnish hotels low due to recession and competition.

- Transport Minister Tuula Linnainmaa says after talks with Russian colleague that Finnish officials may have to take tougher measures if Russia and Finland fail to settle problems in cross-border trucking.
- Swedish clothing retailer Hennes & Mauritz likely to open its first shops in Finland next autumn.
- Parliament's economic committee wants to scrap stamp duty on loans, budgeted to raise one billion markka next year, committee chairwoman Tuulikki Hamalainen says.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Finns did not experience any dramatic decline in mental health during the recession years, research shows.
- International commission investigating the 1994 Estonia ferry disaster says the ship's bow door was not built up to strength specifications, Swedish radio said.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Leading Finnish language lobbyist Seppo Heikinheimo and MP Henrik Lax who chairs the Swedish-speaking Finns' lobby seek way to bring the two language groups closer to each other.
- Finland plans campaign against family violence.
